title: Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines): Cancellation by Tidemark and the Premium It Returns
content:
For **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)**, Tidemark cancels mid-term only for a dishonored payment of the premium or a material misrepresentation in the application, by written notice mailed to the insured giving the tier's insurer cancellation notice period in calendar days from the mailing date to the cancellation date. Tidemark cancels only a policy whose status is active, which the cancellation leaves cancelled; the status is read from the policy record.

On an insurer cancellation the minimum earned premium does not apply: the returned premium is the term premium multiplied by the days from the cancellation date to the term end divided by the days from the term start to the term end, rounded to the cent, with tax and stamping fee returned on it, set first against any amount still owed and only a remaining credit balance refunded.

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Grounds | dishonored payment of the premium; material misrepresentation in the application — no other |
| Notice | written, mailed to the insured, the tier's notice period in calendar days from mailing to cancellation |
| Status | active only |
| Minimum earned premium | does not apply |
| Returned premium | pro rata for the days from the cancellation date to the term end |
| Application of the return | against any amount still owed first; only a remaining credit balance is refunded |

**Worked illustration (hypothetical figures).** A term premium of 1460.00 on a 365-day term, cancelled with 50 days left: the returned premium is 200.00. If 120.00 is still owed on the policy, 120.00 of the return (with its tax and stamping fee figured on 200.00) is set against it first, and only the remaining credit balance is refunded.
